subject: Post-call: streaming throughput & concurrency budget — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: streaming throughput & concurrency budget — next steps

Thanks for the sync earlier — quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on SLOs and the pilot scope. Great context on how you’re using streaming for customer-facing search suggestions.

Key constraints you shared
- Latency target: p95 end-to-end partial-token streaming <= 250 ms (short prompts, sub-50 tokens)
- Typical request size: ~20–40 tokens; some longer diagnostic prompts ~150 tokens
- Steady-state concurrency: ~180 connections; peak during promos ~600 concurrent streaming sessions
- SLA importance: want graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model) rather than hard failures

Redwood performance levers we recommend for the pilot
- Continuous batching + request coalescing for sustained throughput (saves cost, watch tail latency)
- KV/prefix caching for repeat session prompts (big win for chat-like flows)
- Quantization profile: we propose trying an INT8-first profile for the medium model; we’ll run side-by-side quality checks
- Model variants: primary = rwd-medium-stream (quantized), fallback = rwd-small-rt for high concurrency bursts

Immediate asks for the pilot
1) Can you share ~1k sample streaming payloads (short + long) — sample_stream_payloads.jsonl is perfect.
2) Confirm a 2-week pilot window (we propose Apr 4–Apr 15) where we can run perf tests against a dedicated slot.
3) Who will own the quality acceptance? (name + pass/fail criteria)

Attachments: latency_budget_calc.xlsx (budget worksheet)

Proposed next step: I’ll schedule a 30-min slot with Ben (perf lead) and Karthik (solutions/quality) to lock test windows and acceptance criteria.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
[attachment: latency_budget_calc.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming throughput & concurrency budget — next steps

Marissa — noted, thanks. I can run the perf sweep during the Apr 4–15 window. A couple of internal asks before we commit capacity:

- We should get the sample payloads and a short prioritized list of target flows (e.g., search suggestions, long-diagnostic). That will let us craft separate scenarios for short vs long token sequences.
- For the test, do we have permission to use synthetic prefix-caching experiments? (we’ll simulate session reuse patterns to estimate cache hit rates)
- Infra ask: to hit 600 peak concurrency in CI-like conditions we’ll mirror with a 4xGPU dedicated slot for the pilot day runs. Need approvals from infra for reserved capacity.

Tradeoff notes to call out in the runbook:
- Continuous batching increases aggregate throughput and lowers cost/unit but can add 10–80 ms tail latency depending on inter-arrival jitter. We’ll measure p50/p95/p99 delta per batching window.
- Caching gives the best ROI for repeated prompts (session warm-starts). Quantization (int8) will reduce GPU memory and cost by ~30–40% but we must validate output quality on your classification/labeling checks.
- Suggest we set up a canary routing policy so production traffic can fallback to rwd-small-rt when latency spikes.

I’ll start a short internal checklist and loop infra. Karthik — can you own the quality acceptance definition and the human-review plan?

—Ben
Senior Perf Engineer, Redwood Inference
[internal note: reserving perf lab request id PERF-2027-031]

From: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
Cc: ops@fastretail.com
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming throughput & concurrency budget — next steps

Thanks, Marissa — this is helpful and aligns with our expectations. Quick answers and a couple clarifications.

Numbers we can commit to for the pilot
- Latency target: p95 <= 250 ms for partial-token streaming (short prompts). If sustained longer prompts exceed this, we expect graceful fallbacks.
- Peak concurrency: absolute peak historically ~650 but we plan for 600 as a safe bound for pilot testing.
- Steady concurrency: ~150–200 typical outside promotions.
- Average tokens per request: ~30; 10% of traffic is longer diagnostic flows (~120–200 tokens).

We’ll provide the sample_stream_payloads.jsonl (sanitized) and a small quality checklist (10 examples) for side-by-side comparison with quantized model outputs. We are OK with Redwood running synthetic cache-warm experiments — we want a clear description of how you generate the synthetic session patterns.

One ask on quality: if the int8-pilot shows a measurable drop in key metric (click-through relevance >= -2% relative), we’d prefer fallback routing rather than defaulting that model.

Attaching: sample_stream_payloads.jsonl (sanitized)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference>
To: Elena Park <elena@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming throughput & concurrency budget — next steps

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Elena — this is perfect. Finalizing mutual action plan items below so we have ownership and dates.

Mutual action plan (pilot scope)
- FastRetail: provide sanitized sample_stream_payloads.jsonl and a 10-example quality checklist — due Mar 25.
- Redwood: provision 4xGPU dedicated slot for pilot perf runs and run two sweep days (Apr 6 and Apr 12) measuring p50/p95/p99, stream partial-token latency, and cache-hit assumptions. Deliverable: perf dashboard + CSV of raw latency/throughput results (due Apr 16).
- Quality: Karthik will run side-by-side quality evals vs baseline (Karthik to define pass/fail; suggested threshold: CTR degradation <= 2%). Deliverable: quality report (due Apr 18).
- Fallback: configure canary routing so that if the int8 model p95 > 300 ms or quality fails, traffic automatically routes to rwd-small-rt.

I’ll upload a short mutual_action_plan.pdf and share a HubSpot deal card with the pilot milestones. Also linking the DocuSign for the pilot addendum if you want formal signoff: https://docu.sign/FR-pilot-addendum.

Next step: I’ll schedule the 30-min slot with Ben + Karthik to finalize the test harness and confirm infra reservations — proposed times tomorrow 10:00 or 15:00 PT.

Thanks — looking forward to running this pilot.
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference
